acme_pl_support: Hey team — Acme Prod (org: acme) is hitting 401 invalid_api_key from our CI deploys since 10:14 UTC. Dashboard shows the key as "active" and last used earlier today. Sample curl we run in CI:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.run/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-acme","messages": [{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```

Response in CI logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":{"message":"invalid_api_key","type":"authentication_error"}}
```

Repro: same repo + same secret pulled from Secret Manager. Works on dev machine but CI fails. Request-id from CI log: req_0b3c9f7a. Can someone triage? We're blocked on daily deploys.

jessica_support: Thanks — can you paste the masked key prefix (first 6 and last 4 chars) and confirm how the key was created (console/service account/SSO-provisioned)? Also include the full req id and any server side header logs if available. I'll pull logs from our side.

acme_pl_support: Masked prefix: sk-ci1A2b...x9zQ. Key was created by our infra team via the Okta-provisioned service user using the "Create API key" button in the admin UI (we thought it was permanent). Full req id: req_0b3c9f7a-1745604321. We fetch the key in CI with Google Secret Manager via this snippet:

```
SM_ACCESS.getSecretVersion({name: process.env.CI_KEY_SECRET}).payload.data
```

No obvious newline or encoding issues when printed in logs.

tyler_engineer: Pulling the req id now. One quick check: can you confirm whether the key in the Admin UI shows a TTL or mentions "short lived"? There are two flows: permanent service keys and session-scoped keys minted by SSO connector that expire automatically. If it was created from an Okta session context it may be ephemeral.

jessica_support: I see the request in our logs: req_0b3c9f7a -> auth rejected at token validation step. Server-auth logs say: "token_status=revoked at 2024-06-23T10:14:56Z" and "token_source=scim-provisioned". That suggests the key was flagged revoked/short-lived on our backend at time of CI call.

acme_pl_support: Hmm — the key appears in Acme admin as "active" though. How would it show as revoked here? Could Okta/SCIM re-provisioning have replaced the backing credential? Our infra provider mentioned they enabled "rotate on login" for service users recently.

tyler_engineer: Possible scenario: Okta SCIM connector issued a session-scoped secret (TTL ~5m) which the UI accepted but the key in your secret manager was the ephemeral value. Locally you tested immediately after creating (works), CI runs later and token expired -> 401. That matches logs showing "revoked" at the CI timestamp.

jessica_support: Two quick repro checks for you:
1) From a terminal, immediately after creating the key in the Admin UI, run the exact same curl from the CI environment and see if it works. If it does but fails after ~5 minutes, it's ephemeral.
2) In the Admin UI -> API keys, click the key and check if it says "Type: Session (short-lived)" or lists an expiry.

acme_pl_support: Ran check — when we create the key while logged in via Okta, the UI shows a small "session" badge (we missed it). It indeed expires in 5 minutes. Our Secret Manager is caching that value and CI jobs run on schedule ~20m later. My bad.

jessica_support: OK that explains the 401. Short-term fix: rotate CI secret to a permanent service key (Admin -> Create service key -> copy once, store in Secret Manager). If you need a non-console route, we can issue a permanent org-scoped key for you.

tyler_engineer: I've added a server-side check to detect session-scoped keys used from long-lived CI clients and will emit a clearer telemetry message (we currently just return invalid_api_key). I'll file an improvement.

redwood-bot: Created ticket SUP-18224 "CI using short-lived session keys -> 401 on scheduled runs" and linked to this thread.

acme_pl_support: We've created a new permanent service key and updated Secret Manager. CI job ran successfully at 10:58 UTC — no 401s. Request id for the successful run: req_0b3d9a88. Thanks for the fast triage.

jessica_support: Great — closing the immediate blocking issue. Followups: (1) Tyler to add clearer error wording, (2) Docs team to add a note in the API keys docs about Okta/SCIM session keys and CI usage, (3) We recommend customers use "service keys" for CI/dedicated automation.

augie_oncall: Noted — I'll add an alert (SRE) to detect repeated invalid_api_key patterns from CI runners and recommend checking key type. Keeping thread open until docs + telemetry changes are in PR.

acme_pl_support: Thanks all. Please leave the thread open until SUP-18224 is resolved. Confirming last successful deploy looks good.

jessica_support: Will do — marking as "triaged" and tracking on SUP-18224. If anything else pops up ping me.
